title: Methodus generalior numeros quosvis satis grandes perscrutandi utrum sint primi necne?

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E719 tests large N for primality using Euler's idoneal (convenient) numbers. For an idoneal n, a number N = n a^2 + b^2 with gcd(na, b) = 1 is prime if and only if this is its only representation n x^2 + y^2. Here n = 1848 = 8·3·7·11, the largest idoneal number in Euler's table. To avoid subtracting huge multiples 1848x^2, Euler (§63 on the previous page) writes 1848a^2 - (y^2 - b^2) = 1848x^2.

Reduction (previous page):
- Mod 11, y ≡ ±b, and the sign is fixed by replacing y with -y, so he puts y = 22z + b.
- Dividing by 88 gives 21a^2 - ½z(11z+b) = 21x^2.
- So 21 must divide z(11z+b). The factors 3 and 7 can fall on z or on 11z+b, which gives four cases. Writing z(11z+b) = 21pq, each case becomes a^2 - ½pq = x^2.

This page:
- Case IV completed. z = 7q gives 77q + b = 3p. Put s = (q-b)/3, so q = 3s + b, p = 77s + 26b, z = 21s + 7b. The equation is a^2 - ½(3s+b)(77s+26b) = x^2.
- Example (§65). a = 100, b = 197, so N = 1848·10^4 + 197^2 = 18,518,809.
- Case I. z = 21s - 394, shifted by s = 18 + t, so z = 21t - 16 and p = 11t + 1. The test is 10000 - ½(11t+1)(21t-16) = x^2.
  - Values S for t = 0, 1, 2, 3 are -8, 30, 299, 799; for t = -1, -2, -3 they are 185, 609, 1264.
  - First differences are 38, 269, 500, … and 193, 424, 655, …, with constant second difference 231 (= 11·21).
  - Successive differences are subtracted from 10008 until the remainder would go negative. Left column: 9970, 9701, 9201, 8470, 7508, 6315, 4891, 3236, 1350. Right column: 9815, 9391, 8736, 7850, 6733, 5385, 3806, 1996.
  - None is a square.
- Case II (start). S = ½s(231s ± 197) gives 0, 214, 659, 1335 and 17, 265, 744, with differences 214, 445, 676 and 17, 248, 479.

The point: quadratic sequences are scanned for squares using a difference table, needing only additions and subtractions. Every case must be shown to yield no square other than the known x = a, which certifies N prime.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: N, the Case IV parametrisation, the Case I shift, all S values, the differences and every remainder check out, and none of the listed remainders is a perfect square.

Minor looseness: Euler says z > 0 requires s > 18 (strictly s ≥ 19, i.e. t ≥ 1). He nevertheless includes t = 0 and negative t. This is harmless because negative z corresponds to the sign-reversed y and gives the same squares; it only adds redundant checks.
The four cases overlap when 3 or 7 divides both factors. This is harmless redundancy.

ideas.what: Primality certificate via uniqueness of representation N = n x^2 + y^2 for an idoneal n (here 1848)
ideas.where_published: E708, E715, E719, E725 and related papers on numeri idonei; discussed by Weil (Number Theory: An approach through history) and Cox (Primes of the form x^2+ny^2)

ideas.what: Reducing the search by congruence conditions: y ≡ ±b mod 22 and splitting the factors 3 and 7 between z and 11z+b, giving four residue cases
ideas.modern_name: CRT / square-root-of-residue sieving of representations (exclusion-method precursor)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; later Gauss's exclusion method (Disquisitiones, art. 319ff)
ideas.where_published: Same family of idoneal-number papers (E715, E719)

ideas.what: Scanning values of a quadratic polynomial for squares using constant second differences

ideas.modern_name: Euler's large prime from idoneal number 1848
ideas.where_published: E719 itself; the example is cited in secondary literature on idoneal numbers

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct continuation of Euler's well-known idoneal-number primality test with a well-known example (18,518,809). No new idea or unnoticed connection.
transcription_corrections: Case IV equation: the factor is (3s + b), not (5s + b). The text itself gives q = 3s + b; the correct form is aa - ½(3s+b)(77s+26b) = xx.
The section number of 'Exemplum. Sumatur a = 100…' appears in the image as §. 65, not §. 66 (the previous page ended with §. 64). The following 'Pro casu primo' section is §. 66 or 67 (illegible).
Case I left column: the value after 6315 - 1424 is 4891 (the image may look like 4091).
Case I right column: 5385 - 1579 = 3806 (the image may resemble 3706); the next printed value 1996 = 3806 - 1810 confirms 3806.
Case I equation after the shift: z = 21t - 16 and the factor (11t + 1), as transcribed; consistent with p = 11s - b = 11t + 1.
